content:
The image shows banana fruits (pods) with multiple dark, sunken, circular to irregular black/brown lesions on the green skin. The spots are distributed across the body of the fruit, not just at the tip.

Key observations:
- Affected part: banana fruit/pod (not leaves or whole plant)
- Lesions: dark brown/black, sunken, roughly circular spots
- Distribution: scattered across the fruit body, not concentrated at the tip

Reasoning against alternatives:
- Bunchy_Top, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka: all affect leaves, not fruits
- Panama_Disease: vascular wilt affecting whole plant
- Cigar_End_Rot: would specifically affect the blossom-end/tip of the fruit, making it look like ash on a cigar — not matching the scattered body lesions here
- Anthracnose: classic symptom is dark, sunken, circular lesions on banana fruit skin — matches perfectly
